node-1.label: Pruritic and painful periorbital eruption that had lasted 1 month

node-2.label: Patient is a woman in her 70s

node-3.label: Medical history includes lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea

node-4.label: Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine (resulted in retinal toxic effects) and lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 × 10^3/μL)

node-5.label: Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin

attrs.why: New pathologic evidence of left upper eyelid biopsy showing vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, together with expert analyses from the pathologist and laboratory physician, strongly supports cutaneous lupus erythematosus over eczema/seborrheic dermatitis and infection, especially given the known history of lupus nephritis and prior hydroxychloroquine toxicity. Confidence increases from 0.5 to 0.8, though direct immunofluorescence, anti-dsDNA/C3/C4, cultures, and HSV PCR remain unavailable, so some uncertainty persists.

The biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, which is not typical of eczema/seborrheic dermatitis. Both expert analyses state this pattern favors cutaneous lupus over eczematous disease, so confidence decreases from 0.3 to 0.1.

The biopsy findings favor cutaneous lupus over infection, lowering the likelihood of periorbital skin infection. However, the laboratory physician notes that bacterial/fungal culture and HSV PCR remain unavailable and infection is not fully excluded in this immunocompromised patient, so confidence decreases from 0.25 to 0.15 rather than being eliminated.
node-4 past hydroxychloroquine/lenalidomide could cause rash but are past, so weak support; node-5 scaly plaques not specific.
